name: Bun do
summary: Thick red noodles in a pork-and-crab broth, the afternoon bowl on Le Hong Phong. Three published prices do not match. The price now is Check on arrival.
origin: Vietnam National Administration of Tourism and Bao Dak Lak both treat bún đỏ as the bowl that marks Buon Ma Thuot.
howToEat: Vietnam National Administration of Tourism says the orange-red comes from hạt điều, the broth is simmered from bones, and crab roe, shrimp, and minced pork belly are mixed with pepper and shallot and shaped into balls. Eat it with blanched water celery, sweet mustard greens, and bean sprouts, plus pickled onion, pork crackling, shrimp paste, and ground chili. That article puts stalls from about 15:00 or 16:00 and prints 15,000–30,000 VND.

VnExpress on 27 Mar 2021 says the noodles are soaked in broth mixed with dầu điều, and lists thick noodles, a meatball, pieces of crab cake, pork skin, blood, and quail egg, with blanched mustard greens or water spinach and raw herbs. It prints 20,000–35,000 VND, from late afternoon until late evening.

VnExpress on 21 Feb 2016 says the noodles are blanched in water mixed with hạt điều, and prints 20,000–30,000 VND. Bao Dak Lak on 10 Feb 2021 describes a cake of crab, pork, and ground shrimp, quail egg, fried shallot, and pork crackling, in a broth of pork bone, beef bone, and crab, with blanched sweet mustard and water celery rather than a plate of raw herbs. That article prints no price. The close is Check on arrival.
where: Le Hong Phong has a row of stalls. Vietnam National Administration of Tourism names that street. VnExpress on 27 Mar 2021 also names Phan Boi Chau, Phan Dinh Giot, and the night market. VnExpress on 21 Feb 2016 names Phan Dinh Giot and Le Duan. Bao Dak Lak’s photograph is on Phan Dinh Giot. A night-market clock is Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Bun do in Buon Ma Thuot — red noodles on Le Hong Phong
seoDescription: Thick red noodles in a pork-and-crab broth on Le Hong Phong from about 15:00. Published prices do not match. The price now is Check on arrival.
